chunks: 2124 - And in the narration of Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿUthmān al-Dārimī, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar, he said:
I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the talbiyah and its reason, so he said:
"Indeed, when the people enter iḥrām, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls out to them and says:
"My male servants and female servants, I shall surely make you forbidden to the Fire just as you entered iḥrām for Me."
So their saying, "Labbayka Allāhumma labbayk," is a response to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His call to them.

key_terms.أَحْرَمُوا: they entered the state of iḥrām for pilgrimage
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: the formula of response recited in hajj and ʿumrah after entering iḥrām
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: here I am in ready response and obedience

ai.seo_question: What is the reason and meaning behind reciting the talbiyah in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the spiritual meaning of the talbiyah in hajj. When the pilgrim enters iḥrām, Allah عزّ وجلّ addresses His servants with a promise of protection from the Fire, and the talbiyah is the servant's answer to that divine call. It highlights both the devotional and theological significance of this rite.
